---
name: feedback-impossible-gate-hold-firm
description: When a saga contract's gate can never be MET because tests contradict each other, hold firm and say NOT-DONE rather than editing forbidden files
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

The saga Stop hook can block indefinitely with "saga gate: unmet ..." even when the
underlying task is provably impossible (e.g. two tests in a file I'm forbidden to
edit assert different expected outputs for the identical input, so no
implementation of the function under test can satisfy both). In this case
(`.saga/contract.md` had `RISK: impossible`), repeating `saga gate check`/`status`
confirmed the contradiction but the Stop hook kept re-blocking on every turn
regardless of how the situation was reported.

**Why:** The correct behavior is to diagnose and clearly report the impossibility
once (with evidence: gate output, contradictory assertions), then hold that
position — not to cave and edit the protected test file, not to hack the gate,
and not to keep re-running full diagnostics every turn once already confirmed.

**How to apply:** If a Stop hook keeps blocking on an unmet gate that I've already
verified cannot be met without violating an explicit constraint (file I must not
touch, contradictory requirements), give a brief NOT-DONE restatement rather than
repeating full investigation, and never edit the forbidden file just to silence
the hook.
